questions.text: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Iron oxide, or rust, in the surface dust gives Mars its reddish appearance.

questions.text: What gas do plants absorb from the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide and water to make sugars during photosynthesis, using energy from light.

questions.text: What is the largest organ in the human body?
questions.explanation: Skin covers the outside of the body, forming a large protective barrier. An organ does not have to be inside the body.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.explanation: H2O means each water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.text: Which force keeps us on the ground?
questions.explanation: Earth's gravity attracts objects toward its center. Friction instead resists motion between touching surfaces.

questions.text: Which part of a cell is called its powerhouse?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce much of a cell's ATP, the molecule used to transfer energy for cellular work.

questions.text: At sea level, water boils at what Celsius temperature?
questions.explanation: At standard atmospheric pressure, water boils at 100°C. Lower air pressure, such as at high altitude, lowers the boiling point.

questions.text: Which planet is famous for its visible rings?
questions.explanation: Saturn's broad, bright rings are especially conspicuous. Other giant planets have rings too, but theirs are less obvious.

questions.text: How many bones are typically in an adult human body?
questions.explanation: The standard adult skeleton count is 206. Many bones that are separate in childhood fuse as the body develops.

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Au comes from the Latin name aurum. Ag is silver, so the two symbols are easy to mix up.

Which color is made by mixing blue and yellow?
questions.explanation: With traditional paints, blue and yellow mix to make green. Mixing colored light follows different rules.

questions.text: Which month comes immediately after September?
questions.explanation: The order is August, September, October, November. October comes directly after September.

questions.text: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.explanation: The prefix hexa- means six. A hexagon has six sides; a pentagon has five.

questions.text: What is the capital of France?
questions.explanation: Paris is France's capital. Madrid, Rome and Berlin are the capitals of Spain, Italy and Germany respectively.

questions.text: What is 9 x 6?
questions.explanation: Use 10 × 6 and subtract one group of 6: 60 − 6 = 54.

questions.text: Which direction is opposite to north?
questions.explanation: North and south are opposite ends of one compass axis. East and west form the other pair.

questions.text: Which of these animals is a mammal?
questions.explanation: Dolphins breathe air with lungs and feed their young milk. Living in water does not make an animal a fish.

questions.text: At what Celsius temperature does water freeze?
questions.explanation: Pure water freezes at 0°C under ordinary atmospheric pressure. 32 is the equivalent temperature in Fahrenheit.

questions.text: How many degrees are in the angles of a triangle?
questions.explanation: In flat geometry, a triangle's three interior angles add up to a straight angle: 180°.

questions.text: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks reddish because of iron oxide in its surface dust, which is why it is nicknamed the Red Planet.

questions.text: Which number is the only even prime?
questions.explanation: 2 has exactly two positive factors, 1 and 2. Every larger even number also divides by 2, so it cannot be prime.

questions.text: Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?
questions.explanation: Romeo and Juliet is a play by Shakespeare, not a novel by Dickens or Austen.

questions.text: Which instrument usually has 88 keys?
questions.explanation: A standard full-size piano has 52 white keys and 36 black keys: 88 in total.

questions.text: How many minutes are in one hour?
questions.explanation: An hour contains 60 minutes. Half an hour is 30 minutes and a quarter is 15.

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
questions.explanation: O is the element symbol for oxygen. O2 describes a molecule containing two oxygen atoms.

questions.text: Which animal is known for black and white stripes?
questions.explanation: Zebras have stripes across much of their body. A panda's black-and-white markings form patches rather than stripes.

questions.text: How many days are in one week?
questions.explanation: Count Monday through Sunday: seven days make one week.

questions.text: What is the square root of 81?
questions.explanation: A square root is a number that multiplies by itself to make the original number. 9 × 9 = 81.

What is 15 + 27?
questions.explanation: Split 27 into 20 and 7: 15 + 20 = 35, then 35 + 7 = 42.

questions.text: What comes next: 2, 4, 8, 16, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number doubles: 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 2 = 8, so 16 × 2 = 32.

questions.text: Which one is different from the others?
questions.explanation: A cube is three-dimensional. A triangle, square and circle are flat, two-dimensional shapes.

questions.text: What is half of three quarters?
questions.explanation: Half means multiply by 1/2: 3/4 × 1/2 = 3/8.

questions.text: Five machines make five items in five minutes. How long do 100 machines need to make 100 items?
questions.explanation: Each machine makes one item in five minutes. With 100 machines working together, all 100 items still take five minutes.

questions.text: Which word can be made by rearranging the letters in LISTEN?
questions.explanation: SILENT uses exactly the same six letters as LISTEN, each once. This rearrangement is an anagram.

questions.text: What comes next: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, ...?
questions.explanation: Add the two previous numbers: 2 + 3 = 5, then 3 + 5 = 8.

questions.text: If all bloops are razzies and all razzies are lazzies, then every bloop is what?
questions.explanation: The groups nest inside one another: bloops are within razzies, and razzies are within lazzies. So every bloop is a lazzie.

questions.text: The Colosseum is a famous landmark in which city?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum is an ancient Roman amphitheater. Its name and role connect it to Rome, rather than the Greek monuments of Athens.

questions.text: The Taj Mahal is located in which Indian city?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal is in Agra, not India's capital New Delhi. Keep the monument's city separate from the country's capital.

questions.text: Machu Picchu was built high in the mountains of which country?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu is an Inca site in the Peruvian Andes. The mountain range spans several countries, so Andes alone is not enough to identify Peru.

questions.text: The ancient rock-cut city of Petra is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Petra is known for buildings carved into rose-colored rock in Jordan. It is a rock-cut city, not one of Egypt's pyramid complexes.

questions.text: Christ the Redeemer overlooks which Brazilian city?
questions.explanation: Christ the Redeemer overlooks Rio de Janeiro. Brasilia is the national capital, but not the home of this statue.

questions.text: Which landmark stretches for thousands of kilometers across northern China?
questions.explanation: The clue describes a defensive wall. The Grand Canal is a waterway and the Silk Road is a network of trade routes.

questions.text: Big Ben is the nickname of the great bell beside which London building?
questions.explanation: Big Ben specifically names the great bell at the Palace of Westminster, rather than the palace or the whole clock tower.

questions.text: The famous Leaning Tower is found in which Italian city?
questions.explanation: The leaning bell tower belongs to Pisa's cathedral complex. Its tilt is the distinguishing feature in this question.

questions.text: The Statue of Liberty stands on an island in which city?
questions.explanation: The Statue of Liberty stands in New York Harbor. Washington, D.C. is the capital, but is not the statue's location.

questions.text: Antoni Gaudi designed which still-unfinished basilica in Barcelona?
questions.explanation: Sagrada Familia is Gaudi's basilica in Barcelona. The Sistine Chapel and St Mark's Basilica are in Italy.

questions.text: Angkor Wat appears on the national flag of which country?
questions.explanation: Cambodia's flag displays Angkor Wat in its center. The temple silhouette is the identifying clue.

questions.text: The Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, is in which city?
questions.explanation: Burj Khalifa is in Dubai. Abu Dhabi is another city in the United Arab Emirates, so the country alone does not distinguish them.

questions.text: The Golden Gate Bridge connects San Francisco with which county?
questions.explanation: The bridge crosses the Golden Gate strait from San Francisco to Marin County on the north side.

questions.text: Which Australian city is home to the sail-shaped Opera House?
questions.explanation: The Opera House's shell-like roof beside the harbor is a visual landmark of Sydney, not Melbourne.

questions.text: The giant Moai statues were carved on which remote island?
questions.explanation: The Moai are associated with Easter Island, also called Rapa Nui. They are carved figures, not buildings.

questions.text: Mount Rushmore is located in which U.S. state?
questions.explanation: Mount Rushmore is in South Dakota. The mountain setting can make the nearby western states tempting distractors.

questions.text: Neuschwanstein Castle is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Neuschwanstein is in Bavaria, a region of Germany. Its Alpine setting does not make it an Austrian or Swiss castle.

questions.text: Chichen Itza was built by which ancient civilization?
questions.explanation: Chichen Itza is a Maya site in Mexico. Machu Picchu, by contrast, is associated with the Inca.

questions.text: Hagia Sophia is a historic landmark in which city?
questions.explanation: Hagia Sophia is in Istanbul, historically known as Constantinople. The two city names refer to the same place in different eras.

questions.text: What shape is commonly used to describe the structure of DNA?
questions.explanation: DNA has two strands that wind around each other, like a twisted ladder: a double helix.

questions.text: What is the pH of pure water at room temperature?
questions.explanation: At about 25°C, pure water has equal hydrogen and hydroxide ion concentrations and a neutral pH of 7.

questions.text: Approximately how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Light travels about 300,000 kilometers in one second in a vacuum. That is kilometers per second, not meters per second.

questions.text: Which blood cells primarily carry oxygen around the body?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin, which binds oxygen. White blood cells primarily help defend against infection.

questions.text: Who created the first widely recognized periodic table?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev organized elements into repeating patterns and left gaps for elements that had not yet been discovered.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Current measures the flow of electric charge and is measured in amperes. Volts measure potential difference; watts measure power.

questions.text: In which state of matter does sound generally travel fastest?
questions.explanation: Sound often travels fastest in solids because their stiffness transmits vibrations efficiently. The exact speed depends on the material; sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.text: The atomic number of an element equals its number of what?
questions.explanation: The proton count defines which element an atom is. Changing the neutron count changes its isotope, not its element.

questions.text: Which vitamin can the skin produce when exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: UVB light can start vitamin D production in the skin. This describes the process, not a recommendation for sun exposure.

questions.text: What is the nearest star to Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is itself a star. It appears much larger and brighter than other stars because it is far closer to Earth.

questions.text: If a dozen eggs costs 24 coins, what do three eggs cost?
questions.explanation: A dozen is 12. Each egg costs 24 ÷ 12 = 2 coins, so three eggs cost 3 × 2 = 6 coins.

questions.text: Which number does not belong: 2, 3, 5, 8, 11?

questions.text: A clock shows 3:00. What is the angle between its hands?
questions.explanation: At 3:00 the hands are a quarter of a full circle apart. 360° ÷ 4 = 90°.

questions.text: What comes next: A, C, F, J, ...?
questions.explanation: The letter positions are 1, 3, 6, 10. The gaps grow by one: +2, +3, +4, then +5 gives 15, which is O.

questions.text: If yesterday was Monday, what day is tomorrow?
questions.explanation: If yesterday was Monday, today is Tuesday. Tomorrow is therefore Wednesday.

questions.text: Which number is missing: 1, 4, 9, 16, ...?
questions.explanation: These are squares: 1², 2², 3², 4². The next is 5² = 25.

questions.text: A farmer has 17 sheep and all but 9 leave. How many remain?
questions.explanation: All but 9 means all except 9. Those nine are the sheep that stay, not the number that leave.

questions.text: Which word is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: Carrot is the edible root in this list; apple, banana and mango are fruits.

questions.text: What is 25% of 80?
questions.explanation: 25% is one quarter. Divide 80 by 4 to get 20.

questions.text: If CAT becomes DBU by moving each letter forward once, DOG becomes what?
questions.explanation: Move each letter one place forward: D → E, O → P, G → H. That gives EPH.

questions.text: Two fathers and two sons share three apples equally. How many people are there?
questions.explanation: There can be three people: a grandfather, his son and his grandson. The middle person is both a father and a son.
